d.d: Abbreviation of abdomen.
Alternative form of abid
Initialism of all but dissertation.
To surrender, renounce or relinquish, as sovereign power; to withdraw definitely from filling or exercising, as a high office, station, dignity; to fail to fulfill responsibility for.
d.x: to abdicate the throne, the crown, the papacy

d.d: To relinquish or renounce a throne, or other high office or dignity; to renounce sovereignty.
simple past and past participle of abdicate
present participle and gerund of abdicate
The act of abdicating; the renunciation of a high office, dignity, or trust, by its holder.
The voluntary renunciation of sovereign power.
d.x: abdication of the throne, government, power, authority

d.d: Abdomen.
Abdominal.
The belly, or that part of the body between the thorax and the pelvis, not including the back; or in some lower vertebrates, the portion between the cardiac and caudal regions.

The cavity of the belly, which is lined by the peritoneum, and contains the viscera; often restricted in humans to the part between the diaphragm and the commencement of the pelvis, the remainder being called the pelvic cavity.
d.x: He was all bent over complaining of pains in the abdomen.

d.d: The posterior section of the body, behind the thorax, in insects, crustaceans, and other Arthropoda.
Of or pertaining to the abdomen; ventral.
Having the ventral fins under the abdomen and behind the pectoral fins.
Ventral, in describing a fin.
An abdominal muscle.
To take away by force; to carry away (a human being) wrongfully and usually with violence or deception; to kidnap.
To draw away, as a limb or other part, from the median axis of the body.
simple past and past participle of abduct
Having been kidnapped; having become the victim of an abduction.
d.x: Police are searching for an abducted child.

d.d: plural of abductee
present participle and gerund of abduct
A leading away; a carrying away.
The act of abducing or abducting; a drawing apart; the movement which separates a limb or other part from the axis, or middle line, of the body.
A syllogism or form of argument in which the major premise is evident, but the minor is only probable.
plural of abduction
One who abducts; a kidnapper.
A muscle which serves to draw a part out, or from the median line of the body
plural of abductor
third-person singular simple present indicative of abduct
A Muslim.
